newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen stocks end up, influenced by Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen stocks end up, influenced by Shanghai.

text.p: Shenzhen indices ended higher on Monday, dragged up by the Shanghai stock market, brokers said.
But they said Shenzhen had less upward potential than Shanghai because of its already high price levels.
Shenzhen's B share index rose 0.94 points or 0.61 percent to 156.42 on turnover of HK$55.25 million, compared with Friday's HK$88.79 million.
The A share index jumped 6.83 points or 1.73 percent to 402.15 on turnover of 7.00 billion yuan against 7.14 billion yuan on Friday.
"Investors in Shenzhen were encouraged by Shanghai's gains and tried to catch up with the Shanghai market," said one broker. "But Shenzhen's B index is unlikely to rise sharply at such high levels."
Shanghai's B share index put on 0.554 points or 0.81 percent to 69.099 and the A index surged 23.35 points or 2.07 percent to 1,150.39.
"We are going to see slight, steady gains in Shenzhen in the next few sessions, but I don't think it will jump," said an analyst with China Guotai Securities.
Most institutional investors are currently sidelined, waiting for the release of the bulk of companies' 1996 results, analysts said.
Only one B share company out of 43 listed firms in Shenzhen has released 1996 results, with half the result season already passed and the April 30 deadline approaching.
On the B share market, Shenzhen Petrochemical (Holdings) Co Ltd was the best performer, gaining HK$0.16 or 3.72 percent to HK$4.46 with 292,820 shares changing hands.
Shenzhen SEZ Real Estate was the most active counter on volume of 1.03 million shares, up HK$0.13 to HK$4.58, making it the second biggest gainer.

On the A share market, Jiamusi Paper Co Ltd 0699.SZ, which listed 50 million A shares in Shenzhen on Monday, showed the strongest gains and rose to 12.37 yuan from an issue price of 4.70 yuan on volume of 30.6 million shares.
